pr_title: [gh extensions install] Improve help text and error message

issue_context.title: Can't install forked extension
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug I have forked an [extension](https://github.com/IvanRibakov/gh-workflow-stats) and made some improvements. While waiting for the PR to the upstream repo to be reviewed/merged I'd like to share my progress with my colleagues, however I'm unable to install the extension from my fork. ``` gh version 2.54.0 (2024-08-01) https://github.com/cli/cli/releases/tag/v2.54.0 ``` ### Steps to reproduce the behavior I have tried following commands: ``` $ gh extensions install IvanRibakov/gh-workflow-stats $ gh extensions install IvanRibakov/gh-workflow-stats --force $ gh extensions install IvanRibakov/gh-workflow-stats --force --pin f2286ac ``` but all of them return the same cryptic error message: ``` extension is not installable: missing executable ``` ### Expected vs actual behavior Expecting to be able to install an extension from a public fork of a public repo while being able to install the extension from the upstream without issues, instead getting a non-descriptive error. ### Logs

comments:
@williammartin thanks for your help with https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/9760.

I think that can almost allow me to close this one as well. Just one question - what exactly must `--pin` point to?

The docs say:
> pin extension to a release tag or commit ref

but clearly it can't be any commit ref since repo is unlikely to contain a commit with the pre-built binary. Is this commit ref simply used to find the release from which to source the binary?

Hey @IvanRibakov,

Thanks for the detailed bug report. I agree that:

> extension is not installable: missing executable

Is not a very useful error message. Before figuring out what we do next, let me explain how the extension installation works.

First, we check whether there are [installable release artifacts](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/c1939e9c155fec7d08b171ea2bd016c0ea3fc614/pkg/cmd/extension/manager.go#L215) for the given repo and if so, we download the binary and put it in the extension cache. For example, with your upstream extension:

```
➜ gh extension install fchimpan/gh-workflow-stats
✓ Installed extension fchimpan/gh-workflow-stats

➜  ll ~/.local/share/gh/extensions/gh-workflow-stats
total 17432
-rwxr-xr-x@ 1 williammartin  staff   8.5M Oct 15 15:45 gh-workflow-stats
-rw-------@ 1 williammartin  staff   175B Oct 15 15:45 manifest.yml

➜  cat ~/.local/share/gh/extensions/gh-workflow-stats/manifest.yml
owner: fchimpan
name: gh-workflow-stats
host: github.com
tag: v0.3.5
ispinned: false
path: /Users/williammartin/.local/share/gh/extensions/gh-workflow-stats/gh-workflow-stats
```

This is known colloquially as a "binary extension".

If the repo doesn't have a release artifact, then we check whether the given repo contains a [script of the same name](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/c1939e9c155fec7d08b171ea2bd016c0ea3fc614/pkg/cmd/extension/manager.go#L231). If there is a script then we [`clone` the repo into the extension cache](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/c1939e9c155fec7d08b171ea2bd016c0ea3fc614/pkg/cmd/extension/manager.go#L239). For example:

```
➜ gh ext install andyfeller/gh-kraken
⣟Cloning into '/Users/williammartin/.local/share/gh/extensions/gh-kraken'...
⢿remote: Enumerating objects: 43, done.
remote: Counting objects: 100% (43/43), done.
remote: Compressing objects: 100% (31/31), done.
remote: Total 43 (delta 17), reused 29 (delta 7), pack-reused 0 (from 0)
Receiving objects: 100% (43/43), 54.35 KiB | 13.59 MiB/s, done.
Resolving deltas: 100% (17/17), done.
✓ Installed extension andyfeller/gh-kraken

➜  ll ~/.local/share/gh/extensions/gh-kraken
total 136
-rw-r--r--@ 1 williammartin  staff    14B Oct 15 15:49 CODEOWNERS
-rw-r--r--@ 1 williammartin  staff   5.4K Oct 15 15:49 CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
-rw-r--r--@ 1 williammartin  staff   1.1K Oct 15 15:49 LICENSE.txt
-rw-r--r--@ 1 williammartin  staff   2.4K Oct 15 15:49 README.md
-rw-r--r--@ 1 williammartin  staff    40K Oct 15 15:49 banner.webp
-rwxr-xr-x@ 1 williammartin  staff   3.7K Oct 15 15:49 gh-kraken
```

This is known colloquially as a "script extension".

In your case, since you forked a binary extension but your repo doesn't have any of the release assets, it falls back to checking whether you have a script and [then errors when it doesn't find one](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/c1939e9c155fec7d08b171ea2bd016c0ea3fc614/pkg/cmd/extension/manager.go#L235-L237).

As in https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/9760, you can probably understand that it's a bit out of scope for us to build a binary extension.

---

Let me think about what we could do here. Obviously "missing executable" is **very unhelpful** to start with.

> I think that can almost allow me to close this one as well. Just one question - what exactly must --pin point to?

`--pin` means different things depending on whether it is a binary extension or a script extension. As you call out, pinning to a `ref` for a binary extension doesn't make sense. However for a script extension, when we clone the repo locally, we will check out that ref and use the script in there. For example:

```
➜  gh ext install andyfeller/gh-kraken --pin dffcf267059aa0fc9882dd8b837c2c3e40d51768
⣷Cloning into '/Users/williammartin/.local/share/gh/extensions/gh-kraken'...
⡿remote: Enumerating objects: 43, done.
remote: Counting objects: 100% (43/43), done.
remote: Compressing objects: 100% (31/31), done.
remote: Total 43 (delta 17), reused 29 (delta 7), pack-reused 0 (from 0)
Receiving objects: 100% (43/43), 54.35 KiB | 18.12 MiB/s, done.
Resolving deltas: 100% (17/17), done.
✓ Installed extension andyfeller/gh-kraken
✓ Pinned extension at dffcf267059aa0fc9882dd8b837c2c3e40d51768

➜ cd ~/.local/share/gh/extensions/gh-kraken

➜ git show | cat
commit dffcf267059aa0fc9882dd8b837c2c3e40d51768
```

I'm using the term "script" colloquially because really it's just checking if there is a file with the given name in the provided repo. Even though the codebase refers to it as `script`, it could be a binary. It's just that we wouldn't expect binaries to be checked in I suppose.

In any case, I think we could do with:
 * Updating the `help` text to explain what `install` is actually looking for.
 * Updating the `missing executable` error message, though I'll have to think about whether anyone might be relying on the error message in a script.

Thanks for the detailed explanation! 

> Let me think about what we could do here. Obviously "missing executable" is very unhelpful to start with.

It's a pity you had to resort to quoting the source code to explain the extensions mechanism. I have found the Github CLI manual very useful in the past, but it seems that the extensions concept is not as well documented as other (presumably more popular) commands.

> In any case, I think we could do with:

I think that is spot on!

### Acceptance Criteria

**When** I run `gh extension install --help`
**Then** there is an explanation of how `gh` looks to install a remote extension.

See previous comments for details on what that entails.

**Given** I have a repo that does not have a release artifact or script that would be acceptable as an extension
**When** I run `gh extension install <repo>`
**Then** I get an informative error message along the lines of "extension is not installable: no acceptable release artifact or script found in the <repo>"
